newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end down after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end down after quiet day.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended lower after a quiet day dominated by a firm dollar.

In late morning trade, September mark futures mustered enough energy to climb to a session high in positive territory, but the move quickly faded and the contract slipped to new session lows in the afternoon.

Traders tied the brief mark strength to comments from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that stirred intervention worries. But traders said Germany would have to engage in more than just verbal intervention to stem the dollar's steep rise against the mark.
Tietmeyer told Spanish journalists in Frankfurt that he was watching forex developments "very closely."
"For the most part exchange rate developments are the result of corrections which are necessary," Tietmeyer said. "I hope now that it will not come to an overreaction."
Dollar/mark reacted only momentarily to the comments, with support at 1.7850 holding losses.
Earlier, German Finance Ministry official Hansgeorg Hauser said Germany would insist on strict European Monetary Union compliance. He said No EU state can expect to qualify for EMU automatically.

Dollar/yen was strong most of the day, solidly above 116 after overnight dollar-friendly reaction to Japanese trade data. The Japanese trade surplus grew for the third consecutive month in June, but it was below expectations.
September yen slipped to a two-month low overnight, but remained up from those lows during the day session.
Near the close of futures trading, dollar/yen edged back toward the 116 level.
"We had a slow day overall," an IMM currency futures trader said. "The market just shrugged off the numbers this morning and we're looking for trade data tomorrow," he said.
Currency futures' reaction to early U.S. data was muted. The latest weekly jobless claims fell to 349,000 from 377,000 in the previous week and versus a 345,000 forecast.

June housing starts rose 4.8 percent to a 1.452 million annual rate, also in line with expectations. Later, Philadelphia Federal Reserve's July index of business activity rose to 28.1 from 25.2 in June. The forecast had been for a reading of 18.0.
On Friday, U.S. May trade data, June import and export prices and July preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment figures are due.

At the close, September yen futures were down $0.000046 at $0.008685, marks fell $0.0011 to $0.5595, Swiss francs fell $0.0033 to $0.6790, sterling fell $0.0052 at $1.6690, Canadian dollars fell $0.0017 at $0.7284, Australian dollars rose $0.0016 at $0.7381 and Mexican pesos fell $0.000075 at $0.124000.
